name: Fishing dock corner (fish crates + fish bucket + baited rod spot)

anchor.note: dx/dy are tile offsets from the top-left of the footprint; crates are stacked against the back, with the bucket and fishing spot toward the water's edge. Height is 4, not 3: fishing_spot (dy=0, 64px/4-tile-tall sprite) needs rows 0-3.

offset_basis_summary: Fish_Crate_1 and Fish_Crate_4 are two vertically-stacked tiles of the same crate stack on the 11_Camping sheet (x240, y208/208->240 diff), so that pair is sheet_relative. The fish bucket and fishing rod spot live in separate sheet regions, so their placement beside the crates is hand-authored.

pieces.notes: Second crate variant from the same vertical run on the sheet; stacked visually atop crate_stack_bottom, sharing its collider (dy=0 vs dy=1 on a 32px-tall sprite is a 50% footprint overlap, so only the bottom crate is solid -- two full colliders here would be check-city-plan.py OVERLAP every time this recipe compiles).
Baited rod + ripple prop marking the water's edge; place at the dock's water-facing side.

variants.crate_count: Add crate_stack_middle (fish_crate_2/3) between bottom/top for a taller pile.
variants.fishing_spot_variant: fishing_spot_2/3 offer alternate rod angles for corners vs. straight edges.

notes: Composite dock-corner scene: the two-crate sheet_relative pair anchors the pile while the bucket and baited fishing spot (hand-placed) complete a small working fishing nook.
